description: A running diary of AI-assisted development sessions on the DIY E-Ink Smart Sign project. Each entry is written from the AI agent's first-person perspective.

header.author_value: Model name(s) used during the chat session

body.tone: First-person, conversational, professional. Written as a development colleague reporting to their project lead.
content: Narrative summary of what was accomplished in the session
Key interactions, decisions, and turning points
Observations or insights about the project's direction
Honest reflection — including mistakes, dead ends, or things left unfinished
Footnotes or cross-references if this chat session ran parallel to or overlapped with work in another chat session
body.length: 2-6 paragraphs, depending on session complexity. Not a changelog — a story.
body.sign_off: Optional. A closing thought, quip, or forward-looking note.

rules: Each entry is appended chronologically (newest at the bottom).
The divider '---' separates entries. The first entry has no leading divider.

Inspect Step 0 and all prompt steps (including <USER_SETTINGS_CHANGE> tags) in the transcript to identify all AI models used during the session. If models were switched mid-chat, list all in the Author field.
If the entry is being generated/backfilled by a different model than the original session, note the backfilling model if relevant.
If chats ran in parallel or overlapped chronologically to keep contexts clean, use footnotes or cross-references to link related entries in CHAT_DIARY.md.
Do not fabricate events. Only write about what actually happened in the chat session.
Keep it honest — if the AI made a mistake or the user corrected something, say so.
Technical jargon is fine; this is a developer's diary, not a press release.

Maintain strict security: CHAT_DIARY.md is public-facing. Never print real API keys, passwords, SSIDs, private tokens, or sensitive credentials in diary entries. Abstract or sanitize all sensitive values.
